Privacy Policy — Mint Marble (iOS)

Last updated: 29 October 2026

Mint Marble is a single-player marble game for iPhone and iPad, created by Brad Plummer. In this policy, "we" means Mint Marble's developer, the seller shown on Mint Marble's App Store page. Contact: skyflip2026@gmail.com.

Mint Marble is free to play and offers optional one-time in-app purchases: marble finishes, landing effects and Remove Ads. Ads are optional too. Mint Marble can show an occasional full-screen ad only to a player who chose "18 or older", allowed ads, and allowed tracking in Apple's own permission dialog. Everyone else gets the whole game with no ads at all, and the ad software is never started for them. This policy covers your progress and choices, which stay on your device; advertising data, which is processed only if you allow ads and tracking; purchase information, which Apple and Unity's purchasing software handle; and email you send us. Each is described below with how it can be deleted.

1. What the app stores on your device

Mint Marble saves the following in the app's own storage on your device: completed courses, banked stars, course results and best times, the finishes you own and the ones you have equipped, your settings (sound, effects volume, Reduced motion, Steady lanterns), and an unfinished attempt (its course, checkpoint, elapsed time, falls, bumps and the stars collected so far). It keeps spare copies of the save so that an interrupted write can be recovered. It also keeps your age range and your ads choice with the time you made it (section 3); a record of the purchases Apple has verified for this device (section 5); simple ad-pacing counters, such as how many courses you have finished since the last ad (section 4); and the time and the network and ad identifiers of the last ad shown, which "Report an ad" uses (section 4). None of this is uploaded by the game, and we run no servers of our own.

In Settings, "Progress & backups" can copy your progress to the clipboard as text. You choose where to paste and keep it. A backup contains your progress, the unfinished attempt, your settings and the identifiers of your finishes; it never proves or restores a purchase. Copies you keep elsewhere are outside the app, and the app cannot delete them.

Mint Marble does not sync with iCloud. If you back up your device to iCloud or a computer, that backup can include the game's data, as it does for your other apps; backup behaviour is controlled by iOS.

2. What the app does not do

  • No account, login, user name or profile. No chat, user content or social features.
  • No analytics, crash reporting or measurement service of our own. Unity's engine analytics, performance reporting, crash reporting and diagnostics are switched off in the game's configuration.
  • No access to your location, camera, microphone, photos or contacts.
  • The game shows Apple's tracking-permission dialog only to a player who chose "18 or older" and then allowed ads. It never reads your advertising identifier itself.

3. Your age range and your ads choice

On first launch, Mint Marble asks which age range you are in: Under 13, 13 to 17, or 18 or older. You can also tap "Not now", and the game asks again at a later launch. The question asks for no birth date, and the game does not verify the answer. Every answer gives you the whole game. An age answer is not consent to anything. Ads are possible only for players who choose "18 or older". Those players are then asked to choose "Allow ads" or "No ads", shown as equal choices; choosing No ads costs nothing in the game. The age range also decides whether a grown-up check appears before purchases and links (see Children). You can review or change these choices in Settings, under "Ads & Privacy". Once you have made a choice, the game does not ask again at every launch.

4. Advertising — optional, with your permission

When an ad can appear. Mint Marble can show a short full-screen ad (an interstitial) only after you finish a course and tap to continue from its results screen. This happens only occasionally: at most once every four finished courses (falls and retries do not count), with no minimum playing time, and only if an ad is available. Ads never appear during a run, in the Pause menu, at launch, during a stage celebration, or during a purchase or restore. Your stars and progress are saved before any ad.

When the ad software can run. The ad software is Unity LevelPlay with the ironSource Ads and Unity Ads networks, all from Unity Technologies; the ad-quality module is not included. It is started only when all of these hold:

  • you chose "18 or older";
  • you chose "Allow ads" (the same choice is used in every country, as explained below);
  • iOS reports that you allowed tracking;
  • the game has finished checking your purchases with Apple, and you do not own Remove Ads.

In every other case, the ad software is not started and no ad is requested. That includes players under 18, players who have not answered, players who declined or withdrew, and players for whom tracking is denied, restricted or not yet answered. There is no fallback to other kinds of ads.

The same choice is used worldwide. In the European Economic Area and the United Kingdom, "Allow ads" is your consent to the advertising data use described here. In US states with privacy laws, allowing ads permits this advertising data use and sharing, and choosing "No ads" or withdrawing later is your opt-out. Apple's tracking permission is a separate, additional requirement.

What it collects and why. Once you have allowed ads and tracking, the ad software sends the following to Unity and ironSource:

  • your device's advertising identifier (IDFA) and Apple's identifier for vendors;
  • your IP address and the country derived from it;
  • device and app information (model, iOS version, language, screen size, connection type, app version);
  • ad activity (ads requested, shown, clicked and closed) and performance data about the ad software.

Unity's own disclosure for the Unity Ads network also lists an SDK-level user identifier and purchase history among the data that network may process. A report you make through an ad's own controls goes to Unity. The networks use this data to choose, personalize and measure ads, to pay for ads, to prevent fraud and to operate the ad service. Choosing and measuring ads includes linking the data with data from other companies' apps and sharing it with advertising partners and attribution companies. That is "tracking" in Apple's sense, which is why iOS asks for your permission first.

For a player who allowed ads and tracking, the game tells the ad software three things: that you consented to advertising, that you have not opted out of sale or sharing, and that you are not a child. It never sends those signals for anyone else. The game's configuration also lists ad-network identifiers for Apple's SKAdNetwork, Apple's privacy-preserving ad-attribution system, which involves no identifier about you. Unity's practices and retention are described in its policies: unity.com/legal/privacy-policy and unity.com/legal/game-player-and-app-user-privacy-policy (ironSource is part of Unity). We do not receive personal information from the ad software; we receive only aggregated reports.

Changing your mind. In Settings, "Ads & Privacy" lets you change your age range, switch ads off or on, and reach Apple's tracking setting. Switching ads off, changing your age range to under 18, turning tracking off in iOS (Settings, then Privacy & Security, then Tracking), or buying or restoring Remove Ads all have the same effect. The game tells the ad software that consent is withdrawn and that you opt out of sale or sharing, discards any ad it holds, requests nothing further, and does not start the ad software at later launches. An ad already on screen finishes normally. Ad software that has already started cannot be shut down inside the running session, because its maker offers no such control; it stops when the app is closed. If you later allow ads again and every condition above holds, ads can resume in the same session. While the game is checking your purchases with Apple, no ad is requested.

Reporting an ad. If an ad seems inappropriate, use Report an ad in Settings, under "Ads & Privacy". It prepares an email to us with the app version, the time of the last ad and that ad's network, ad unit, instance, creative and auction identifiers; it includes no device identifier or age answer, and nothing is sent unless you send the email. We pass reports on to the ad provider.

5. Purchases (Apple and Unity In-App Purchasing)

Mint Marble sells marble finishes, landing effects (the six pastel landings as one set) and Remove Ads as one-time purchases through Apple's App Store, with your Apple Account. The Original Chrome marble and the Mint Ripple landing are always free. Finishes change only the look; every marble handles the same. Prices come from Apple in your local currency. We never see or store your payment details.

When you buy or restore, Apple gives the game a signed transaction record. The game uses it only to unlock what you bought and keeps the local ownership record described in section 1. Restore Purchases, in Settings under "Purchases", asks Apple to resynchronize your purchases for the same Apple Account. It never charges you again, and it does not restore progress or settings. Refunds are handled by Apple: a refunded item is removed from your collection, and after a refund of Remove Ads, the ad choices in section 4 apply again.

Purchases are handled with Unity Technologies' In-App Purchasing software ("Unity IAP"). Unity IAP sends purchase events to Unity when you start, cancel, fail or complete a purchase, and when a purchase that was paid but not yet delivered completes later (for example, after an Ask to Buy approval). These events include the product, its price and currency, Apple's transaction identifiers and signed transaction information, the game's bundle identifier and version, device information (model, iOS version, language and region settings, time since the device was started, and storage size) and Apple's identifier for vendors. Unity's privacy documentation for Unity IAP also lists the country among the data it collects. Unity processes this data to operate the purchasing service on our behalf and, under its own policy, for its financial reporting and auditing, legal compliance, security and fraud prevention. No such event is sent when you only open the game, browse or preview items, or restore purchases. The game reports no purchase to the ad software.

6. Email you send us, and this website

The "Privacy policy" link in the app opens this website in your browser. "Contact support" and "Report an ad" open an email draft in your mail app; nothing is sent unless you send it. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages. The pages themselves set no cookies and contain no analytics or third-party content. GitHub, the host, logs and stores the IP address of every visitor for security purposes, whether or not the visitor is signed in to GitHub (GitHub's documentation: "When a GitHub Pages site is visited, the visitor's IP address is logged and stored for security purposes, regardless of whether the visitor has signed into GitHub or not" — docs.github.com). That logging is done by GitHub under GitHub's Privacy Statement, not by us, and we do not receive those logs.

If you email us at skyflip2026@gmail.com, we receive your email address and whatever you choose to write or attach, including any backup text or ad report. We use it only to handle your request and reply to you. Please do not send passwords. We keep correspondence about this game for at most 12 months after your request is resolved, and delete it earlier when it is no longer needed. There are two narrow exceptions. If an issue you raised is still open, we keep that thread until it is resolved, and the 12-month limit runs from then. If a law requires us to keep a particular message for longer, we keep that message only as long as the law requires.

You can ask us to delete your correspondence with us about this game at any time by emailing the same address. Please put "Deletion request" in the subject line so we can find it. We handle deletion requests separately from routine support, and where a law sets a deadline for answering such a request, that deadline applies.

Deleting your data — by kind

  1. On your device. Deleting Mint Marble removes its saved progress, settings, age range, ads choice and purchase record from that device. "Offloading" the app (an iOS feature) removes the app but keeps its documents and data, so everything returns if you reinstall. Purchases stay with Apple and come back through Restore Purchases on the same Apple Account; refunded purchases do not. Text backups you copied elsewhere are yours to delete. Device backups are controlled by iOS, and we make no promises about them.
  2. Advertising data held by Unity. Unity holds the advertising data (section 4) under its own policies, which describe how to access or delete it. We do not receive it.
  3. Purchase data held by Unity. For the purchase data Unity processes on our behalf (section 5), email us at skyflip2026@gmail.com with "Deletion request" or "Access request" in the subject line, and we will pass the request to Unity, which handles such requests manually. For data Unity uses for its own purposes, Unity asks you to contact it directly at unity-iap-contact@unity3d.com (Unity's address, not ours).
  4. Email. Emails you exchanged with us about this game are deleted on request at skyflip2026@gmail.com. Otherwise they are deleted at most 12 months after your request is resolved (earlier when no longer needed), subject to the two narrow exceptions in section 6.

Children

Mint Marble is made for a general audience that includes children. It is not primarily directed at children and is not offered in the App Store's Kids category. Players under 18, and players who have not given their age, never get ads: the ad software is never started for them, and the game never asks them about tracking. We do not collect personal information through the app ourselves. Purchases go through Apple, which offers family controls such as Ask to Buy, and through Unity's purchasing software (section 5). Players who chose Under 13 or 13 to 17, and players who have not answered, see a grown-up check before purchases, Restore Purchases and links out of the app. If you are a parent and believe your child has sent us personal information by email, contact us at skyflip2026@gmail.com and we will delete it.

Changes

If this policy changes, we will update this page and its date before the changed version of the game is released.
